items.title: Anteris Announces Upcoming Data Release for Medium-Size DurAVR THV from EMBARK Study at TCT 2026
items.title_zh: Anteris将在TCT 2026公布中号DurAVR生物仿生瓣膜EMBARK研究首批30天数据
items.summary_zh: 2026年10月27日,Anteris Technologies宣布将在10月31日至11月3日于圣地亚哥举行的TCT 2026大会上,首次公布其生物仿生球囊扩张式经导管主动脉瓣DurAVR中号型号在EMBARK研究中的30天临床及血流动力学结果,由Azeem Latib医生于11月1日在Innovation Theater环节报告。此前该瓣膜已在全球EMBARK研究及美国早期可行性研究(EFS)中为130余名患者植入各尺寸型号。DurAVR采用单层生物仿生瓣叶设计,旨在恢复更接近天然主动脉瓣的层流血流模式,公司计划以此数据支持其正在美欧同步招募约1000例患者的PARADIGM全球关键性随机对照试验。
items.summary_en: On October 27, 2026, Anteris Technologies announced that Dr. Azeem Latib will present the first 30-day clinical and hemodynamic outcomes for the medium-size DurAVR biomimetic balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve from the EMBARK study, in the Innovation Theater at TCT 2026 (San Diego, Oct 31-Nov 3). Since 2021, more than 130 patients have been treated with DurAVR across valve sizes in the EMBARK study and a US Early Feasibility Study; the single-leaflet biomimetic design aims to restore more native-like laminar flow, and the data will support the ongoing roughly 1,000-patient PARADIGM global pivotal randomized trial now enrolling in the US and Europe.

items.title: GrOwnValve Achieves Primary Safety Endpoint in First-in-Human Heart Valve Study
items.title_zh: GrOwnValve自体再生肺动脉瓣首次人体研究达到主要安全性终点
items.summary_zh: 2026年10月26日,德国GrOwnValve公司宣布其基于患者自体心包组织构建的可生长经导管肺动脉瓣,在柏林夏里特医学院开展的首次人体可行性试验(GECT-DZHK28,NCT05809856)中,首批5例完成6个月随访的患者均达到预设主要安全性终点——未发生瓣膜相关死亡、大出血、再次手术或急性器械相关并发症。该研究计划共纳入7名患有先天性肺动脉瓣疾病的青年患者,首例病例已发表于《European Heart Journal - Case Reports》。由于样本量仅5例、随访时间仅6个月,这一结果只是早期安全性信号,瓣膜能否随患者生长及长期耐久性仍待进一步观察。
items.summary_en: On October 26, 2026, Germany's GrOwnValve announced that its first-in-human feasibility study (GECT-DZHK28, NCT05809856) of an autologous, pericardium-derived, growable transcatheter pulmonary heart valve met its primary safety endpoint: none of the first five patients, who completed six-month follow-up at Charite - Universitatsmedizin Berlin, experienced device-related death, major bleeding, reoperation, or acute device-related complications. The trial plans to enroll seven young adults with congenital pulmonary valve disease, and the first case was published in European Heart Journal - Case Reports. With only five patients and six months of follow-up, this is an early safety signal rather than evidence of the valve's growth potential or long-term durability.
